sao-marcos.name: São Marcos Church and Hospital
sao-marcos.short: A Baroque hospital façade with statues of the apostles; a hotel now fills the former wards
sao-marcos.long: Archbishop Diogo de Sousa founded the São Marcos hospital in 1508. In the 18th century Carlos Amarante gave it a church with two towers and a long façade with statues of the apostles on the balustrade. The hospital treated the townspeople until 2011. Since 2018 a hotel has occupied its north wing, while the church still belongs to the Misericórdia brotherhood.
sao-marcos.history:
The place has a long history. Archbishop Rodrigo da Cunha recorded a tradition: the Templar master Gualdim Pais brought the relics of Saint John Mark back from the Holy Land. The relics were placed in a chapel, became famous for healing, and a shelter for the sick grew up beside it. In 1508 Archbishop Diogo de Sousa replaced three small shelters with a single hospital, São Marcos. In 1559 Archbishop Bartolomeu dos Mártires handed it to the brotherhood of the Santa Casa da Misericórdia, which ran it until 1975.

In the 18th century the north wing and the church were built to a design by Carlos Amarante. The side wings were designed and built by the stonemason José Fernandes da Graça, known as Landim. Work on the church stalled for long periods. From 1794 it continued with money from Archbishop Caetano Brandão, who in 1798 also opened a surgical school at the hospital.

What to look for on the façade. The church’s two towers rise above a long, symmetrical block. Full-length figures line the balustrade: the apostles Peter, Andrew, John and James, and other saints. In the niche above the entrance stands Saint Mark in a bishop’s vestments. Inside are a gilded main altar, a painted dome and a stone reliquary with the Latin inscription “Sacred bones of the divine John Mark”.

The façades of the hospital and church have been a Property of Public Interest since 1956. The hospital worked until 2011, when Braga’s new hospital opened. The Misericórdia leased part of the buildings to the Vila Galé hotel chain. The 123-room hotel opened in 2018, and its wings are named after three archbishops. The church, the São Bento chapel and the Misericórdia’s pharmacy were not part of the hotel.
facts: Archbishop Diogo de Sousa founded the hospital in 1508.
The church and the north wing were built to a design by Carlos Amarante.
The hospital took in the sick for more than 500 years, until 2011.
A 123-room hotel opened in the former hospital in 2018.
The façades of the hospital and church have been a Property of Public Interest since 1956.
sao-marcos.tip: The church stands on Praça Carlos Amarante, next to the Raio Palace. Entry is free, but it opens only briefly: about an hour in the morning on weekdays and Sundays, and it is closed on Saturdays. Check the hours on the Visit Braga website. The façade with its statues is best seen from the small garden in front of it.
